statement: When NVMe reads are the throughput bottleneck and the existing pipeline already overlaps H2D copies with I/O (sliding-window), eliminating the H2D copy via GPUDirect/nvidia-peermem provides zero throughput improvement. The H2D copy is fully hidden behind NVMe latency and is not on the critical path.
regime: Single NVMe Gen4 drive (~2.4 GB/s random 4MiB read throughput), 4MiB objects, sliding-window pipeline with queue depth 16, H2D copy time (~0.5ms) << NVMe read time (~1.7ms)
mechanism: The sliding-window pipeline (validated in RP-2) submits the next NVMe read immediately after each completion, then issues the H2D copy asynchronously. Since NVMe read latency (1.7ms for 4MiB) exceeds H2D copy time (0.5ms for 4MiB at 8 GB/s PCIe), the H2D copy always completes before the next NVMe read finishes. The H2D copy occupies zero wall-clock time from the pipeline's perspective. Removing it (via NVMe→GPU direct DMA) cannot recover time that was never spent waiting.
applicability_bounds: Applies when: (1) single-drive throughput is the bottleneck, (2) object size is large enough that NVMe latency >> H2D latency (4MiB at Gen4 speeds), (3) sliding-window pipeline is already overlapping I/O with copies. Does NOT apply when: multiple drives saturate PCIe bandwidth (H2D would then contend for PCIe with NVMe traffic), or object size is very small (NVMe latency ≈ H2D latency, copy becomes visible).

statement: nvidia-peermem + spdk_mem_register on GPU device pointers (including IPC-opened handles) successfully enables NVMe DMA writes directly to GPU memory. The mechanism is functional but concurrent registrations from multiple threads cause data corruption in batch workloads (all entries receive the last-registered entry's data).
regime: SPDK userspace NVMe driver, nvidia-peermem kernel module loaded, GPU memory from cudaMalloc/cudaIpcOpenMemHandle, concurrent spdk_mem_register from 2+ threads on different GPU pointers
mechanism: spdk_mem_register calls nvidia_p2p_get_pages via nvidia-peermem to map GPU physical pages into the IOMMU. When called concurrently from multiple threads on different GPU pointers, the IOMMU mapping updates are not atomic — the last registration overwrites translations for previously-registered regions. NVMe DMA then targets the physical address of the last-registered GPU pointer for ALL in-flight reads. Sequential (single-threaded) use works correctly.
applicability_bounds: The corruption only manifests when spdk_mem_register is called concurrently from multiple threads. Single-threaded sequential register→read→unregister cycles work correctly. A global lock around register/unregister would fix correctness but introduces deadlock risk with SPDK's reactor model. The practical workaround is to pre-register all GPU memory regions before starting parallel NVMe reads.

statement: For single-drive NVMe-to-GPU cold path optimization, the binding constraint is NVMe read bandwidth (~2.4 GB/s random 4MiB from a single Gen4 SSD), not the data transfer architecture (DRAM bounce vs. direct GPU DMA). The path to higher throughput requires multi-drive parallelism.
regime: Single NVMe Gen4 SSD, 4MiB random reads, SPDK userspace driver, any GPU (PCIe Gen4 x16)
mechanism: A single Gen4 NVMe SSD delivers ~2.4 GB/s for random 4MiB reads (below theoretical 7 GB/s sequential due to access pattern and FTL overhead). PCIe Gen4 x16 bandwidth to GPU is ~25 GB/s (upstream). The NVMe→DRAM→GPU path uses ~4.8 GB/s of PCIe bandwidth (2.4 GB/s upstream NVMe→DRAM + 2.4 GB/s downstream DRAM→GPU), well within the PCIe fabric capacity. Eliminating one traversal cannot increase throughput when the source (NVMe) is the bottleneck.
applicability_bounds: The NVMe-bottleneck regime holds for 1-2 drives. At 3+ Gen4 drives (~7.2+ GB/s aggregate read), the PCIe topology and DRAM bandwidth start to matter. Multi-drive scaling may benefit from P2P (fewer PCIe hops), especially when NVMe and GPU share the same PCIe switch.

statement: GPUDirect P2P (NVMe→GPU BAR1 DMA) with a staging ring buffer is dramatically slower than zero-copy DRAM (NVMe→pinned DRAM→async H2D) regardless of pipeline pattern, because there is no efficient CUDA path to move data from externally-DMA'd BAR1 GPU memory to another GPU allocation.
regime: GDRCopy BAR1 staging approach, any pipeline pattern, any object size
mechanism: GDRCopy maps GPU memory to BAR1 VA for CPU access. NVMe DMA to BAR1 VA succeeds but the resulting GPU memory state is invisible to CUDA (L2 cache stale, no coherent path from BAR1-staged region to VRAM). D2D copies read stale cache; CPU backfill from BAR1 is 47% slower due to PCIe latency per access.
applicability_bounds: Only applies to the GDRCopy BAR1 mechanism. Does NOT apply to nvidia-peermem direct registration (RP-6), which writes to the actual GPU device memory via IOMMU.

statement: Batch-based ring buffer pipelines (submit all → wait all → copy all → sync) are significantly slower than sliding-window pipelines (overlap reads with copies) for sequential NVMe-to-GPU transfers.
regime: Sequential NVMe transfers of large objects (>128KiB), any target memory (DRAM or GPU)
mechanism: Sliding-window pipelines submit the next NVMe read immediately after each completion, overlapping I/O with copy operations. Batch pipelines serialize phases, leaving the NVMe idle during copy phases.
applicability_bounds: The benefit is proportional to the ratio of copy time to read time. When copy time approaches zero (as in the P2P direct path), both patterns converge to the same throughput.

statement: CPU memcpy from GPU BAR1 VA to DRAM adds approximately 47% overhead to the P2P cold path due to high per-access PCIe latency when reading GPU BAR1 memory from CPU.
regime: GDRCopy BAR1 mapped memory, CPU read access, any block size
mechanism: Each CPU load from BAR1 VA triggers a PCIe read transaction (non-posted, must wait for response). The per-access latency (~500ns) dominates when reading large buffers byte-by-byte or word-by-word.
applicability_bounds: Only applies to CPU reads from BAR1 VA (GDRCopy path). Not relevant to nvidia-peermem path (no BAR1 involved).

statement: External PCIe DMA writes to GPU BAR1 memory do not invalidate the GPU L2 cache; subsequent CUDA D2D copies from the dev_ptr associated with that BAR1 region read stale data.
regime: NVMe DMA to GDRCopy-mapped BAR1 VA, subsequent CUDA kernel or D2D copy from the same dev_ptr
mechanism: GPU L2 cache is not coherent with PCIe writes to BAR1. DMA writes bypass L2, but CUDA reads from the associated dev_ptr hit stale L2 entries.
applicability_bounds: Only applies to GDRCopy BAR1 path. nvidia-peermem direct registration (RP-6) writes to the same physical memory that CUDA sees, maintaining coherence because the DMA targets the GPU's device memory directly (same path as GPU's own memory controller).
